liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (3 reviews): A short instrumental Nobody's Fault but Mine appears in the Truckin' exit jam; Truckin' leads into a long Nobody's Fault but Mine jam [16][17][18]
- **Candyman** (2 reviews): Reviewer especially likes the Candyman and Althea performances; Jerry's opening of his Candyman solo is singled out as a good one [10][14]
- **Althea** (2 reviews): Jerry's playing on Althea is praised as very nice; Set one closes with Althea > Lost Sailor > Deal, which the reviewer enjoys [15][20]
- **Lost Sailor** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Lost Sailor as a favorite, saying it is displayed well in this performance; Reviewer calls Althea and Lost Sailor excellent [10][14]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Phil is described as over the top in Shakedown Street [15]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer picks the He's Gone into The Other One sequence as a highlight [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **It's raining like hell outside**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-08-13.178895.sony.ecm270.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 162 min [1]
- **gd1979-08-13.154846.akg.5se.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 20 songs; 161 min [3]
- **gd1979-08-13.mtx.seamons.123208.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 163 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [5]
- **gd79-08-13.sbd.clugston.9289.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 157 min; rated 4.22/5 by 9 [7]. Said about its sound: This copy's second set seems to have lost high end, probably from improper noise reduction; older cassette generations sound better; Reviewer finds the Clugston upgrade strong-sounding, with good quality; Sound is somewhat degraded but still very listenable [12][13][14]

## Around the show

- Reviewer notes Brent's keyboard playing sounds funky throughout the show [15]
- Some lyrics were forgotten in Candyman and El Paso, but were smoothly covered [20]
- Reviewer has only a first-set soundboard and says the second set is hard to find; the show aired on Sirius [21]
- Reviewer says the I Need a Miracle > Bertha > Good Lovin' medley was typical of this great era [17]
- Reviewer says the I Need a Miracle > Bertha > Good Lovin' medley was typical of this great era [18]
- Pairs well with the second set of the 8/14 show as a two-disc set [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-08-13.178895.sony.ecm270.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM-270 mics > Sony TC-158SD (Maxell UDXLII) [1]. Also: A 12-second patch in Drums comes from a Nakamichi 700 source [1]
- **gd1979-08-13.154846.akg.5se.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [3]. Also: Nakamichi 700 source patches several spots, including Me & My Uncle, El Paso, He's Gone, Drums > Wharf Rat, and Truckin'; A soundboard source supplies an 8-second patch in the Other One > Drums transition [3]
- **gd1979-08-13.mtx.seamons.123208.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) [5]
- **gd79-08-13.sbd.clugston.9289.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [7]. Also: A Clugston upgrade of this show circulates, according to the reviewer [13]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1979-08-13 Mon McNichols Sports Arena, Denver, CO](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1291362411379/grateful-dead-1979-08-13-mon-mcnichols) [23]
- Fan art by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1979-08-13 Mon McNichols Sports Arena, Denver, CO](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1291362411379/grateful-dead-1979-08-13-mon-mcnichols) [24]
